2: For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David. I said, “I will guard my ways ⌞that I may not sin⌟ with my tongue. I will keep a muzzle over my mouth as long as the wicked are before me.”
3: I was mute with silence. I was silent even from saying good things, and my pain was stirred up.
4: My heart grew hot inside me; in my sighing a fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue,
5: “Let me know, O Yahweh, my end, and what is the measure of my days. Let me know how transient I am.”
6: Look, you have made my days mere handbreadths, and my lifespan as nothing next to you. Surely every person standing firm is complete vanity. Selah
7: Surely a man walks about as a mere ⌞shadow⌟; surely in vain they bustle about. He heaps up possessions but does not know who will gather them in.
8: And now, O Lord, for what do I wait? My hope is for you.
9: From all my transgressions deliver me; do not make me the taunt of the fool.
10: I am mute. I do not open my mouth, for you, yourself, have done it.
11: Remove from me your affliction. By the opposition of your hand I perish.
12: When with rebukes you chastise a man for sin, you ⌞consume⌟ like a moth his delightful things. Surely everyone is a mere vapor. Selah
13: Hear my prayer, O Yahweh, and listen to my cry for help; do not be deaf to my tears. For I am an alien with you, a sojourner like all my ancestors.
14: Look away from me that I may be cheerful, before I depart and I am no more.
